report:
Reviewed the full fresh crates.sage_ir.types.body.macro_expansion claim and all implementation/test associations. The claim requires checked expressions to represent the output of expression macro expansion and prohibits presenting an invocation itself as a successful checked expression node. Positive expansion-output behavior and the negative successful-output restriction are distinct requirements; resolving a macro name or retaining its token tree is insufficient.

The sole implementation association is the explicit sage_meta::todo marker in crates/sage-meta/tests/representation_spec.rs, documenting pending expression macro expansion and whole-tree rejection of unexpanded macro nodes. The only associated test, sage_meta::todo::types_body_macro_expansion, repeats that prerequisite and contains no assertions. No ordinary implementation or test entry claims completed behavior, and no N/A exemption is used. Running the placeholder would not establish either requirement.

Captured the current TyExprData representation: it still includes MacroCall with a resolution and token tree alongside Error, Unresolved and Missing. A transitional invocation representation is not proof of checked expansion output, and its existence alone is not proof that a successful public body exposes it. The TODO expressly retains both expression expansion and the whole-tree rejection work needed to establish the boundary. Captured checker context includes diagnosed Missing syntax recovery; that is not treated as expression macro support or evidence of successful expansion. This review makes no unsupported claim about all parser or expansion paths.

Captured the typed-IR completed-body design and accepted architectural-foundations rationale. They require resolved typed trees and distinguish error recovery from ordinary success. These design statements support the intended boundary but do not supply executable coverage. Replacing the deferral requires expression expansion to produce checked output nodes and associated fixtures that directly inspect expansion semantics, traverse nested expression output to reject retained invocations, and distinguish unsupported/error expansion from successful output. Item/derive expansion or a resolved macro identity cannot substitute for these expression-specific checks.

All aspects are accounted for as explicitly deferred, with the unchanged claim preserved. Validation was source inspection through review start/read; no source edits or behavioral tests were performed. Coordinator-run suites remain separate evidence. No requested edits: the current TODO clearly identifies the implementation and test prerequisites without claiming completion.
